title: Parametrized end-Yoneda for coherent corepresentable weights
statement:
Use universes, quasicategories and coherent transformations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the space category of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], the concrete coherent Hom pairing of [def-coef-infinity-presheaf-yoneda], and the twisted-arrow projection $(s,t)$ of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration]. Let $C,L$ be $\mathcal V$-small quasicategories, $c:L^{\mathrm{op}}\to C$ a coherent functor, and $T:C\times L\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ an arbitrary coherent functor. Define the corepresentable weight $W_c:C\times L\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ by $W_c(x,l)=\operatorname{Map}_C(c(l),x)$, using the concrete coherent Hom pairing and restriction along $c$; any coherently equivalent family with the corresponding identity points is also allowed. Define $D:L^{\mathrm{op}}\times L\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ by $D(l,l')=T(c(l),l')$. There is an equivalence of whole mapping spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C\times L,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})}(W_c,T)\simeq\lim_{(l\to l')\in\operatorname{Tw}(L)}T(c(l),l').$$
The right side is the coherent space-valued limit of $D\circ(s,t)$. Its projection at $1_l$ sends $\tau$ to $\tau_{c(l),l}(1_{c(l)})$. Conversely, if a point of this limit is a coherent cone $z$ and $z_l$ is its projection at $1_l$, the inverse has component $\tau_{x,l}(f)=T(f,1_l)(z_l)$ for $f:c(l)\to x$. This formula denotes coherent evaluation and action, with all higher data supplied by the equivalence. The equivalence and its inverse homotopies are natural in $T,c$, in restriction of the parameter category $L$, and in additional simplicial parameters. All functor categories are formed in a containing universe, the limit admits a $\mathcal V$-small model, and empty $C$ and $L$ are allowed. No Kan extension, restriction adjunction, or density assertion is assumed.

source.place: Agent-formulated parametrized end-Yoneda consequence of Theorem 5.8.13(ii), printed pp.259-261, and the coherent-end formula of Kerodon Example 8.3.4.22 (03P7), https://kerodon.net/tag/03P7. Formula (5.8.8.4) and Theorem 5.8.9 specify identity evaluation; 5.8.13 supplies joint naturality. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copies WANTED. No Stacks tag states this assertion.

proof.text: Restrict the concrete Hom pairing of [def-coef-infinity-presheaf-yoneda] along $c$ in its first variable. An arrow $l\to l'$ gives $c(l')\to c(l)$ and hence precomposition $\operatorname{Map}_C(c(l),x)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(c(l'),x)$. Swapping the factors gives exactly the coherent functor $W_c:C\times L\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$. Use the containing-universe conventions of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. For an allowed equivalent weight $W'_c\simeq W_c$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] inside the functor quasicategory: precomposition by the equivalence edge and its inverse give maps of whole mapping spaces; associativity, the two inverse triangles and the unit homotopies show that their composites are homotopic to the identities. Thus it suffices to use the concrete weight, and its specified identity points are preserved.

source.place: Construction (5.8.8.4), Theorem 5.8.9 and Theorem 5.8.13(ii), printed pp.257,259-261; agent expansion separating coherent evaluation from its pointwise invertibility.

proof.text:
Apply the product/Fubini clause of [lem-coef-coherent-end-twisted-arrow-formula] with first shape $C$, second shape $L$, target $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$, and $F=W_c$, $G=T$. It gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C\times L,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})}(W_c,T)\simeq\lim_{(l\to l')\in\operatorname{Tw}(L)}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})}(W_c(-,l),T(-,l')).$$
This is an equivalence of whole spaces with coherent indexed diagram, identity-component evaluation and a $\mathcal V$-small Kan model, also for empty shapes.

source.place: Example 8.3.4.22; coherent-end formula and its product/Fubini consequence.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal F=\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$ and $A:C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal F$ be the exponential transpose of the concrete pairing in [def-coef-infinity-presheaf-yoneda], so $A(a)(x)=\operatorname{Map}_C(a,x)$. The final compatibility clause of [lem-coef-cone-straightening-coherent-evaluation] expressly identifies this concrete pairing as the canonical rigidification model of the coherent Hom bifunctor, comparing it with right-pinched mapping spaces, their actions and all higher data, and preserving the underlying edge. Use that model and its identity comparison in the end theorem. Apply [lem-coef-coherent-end-twisted-arrow-formula] to $F=G=\mathrm{id}_C:C\to C$, using this coherent Hom model. The identity point of $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,C)}(\mathrm{id}_C,\mathrm{id}_C)$ gives a point of $\lim_{\operatorname{Tw}(C)}\operatorname{Map}_C(s(-),t(-))$, equivalently a coherent section $\xi:*\to B_A\circ(s,t)$. The component-evaluation clause and the identity comparison give $\xi_a=1_a$ at each $1_a$, with the specified unit homotopy. All higher data are supplied by that one coherent section.

source.place: Example 8.3.4.22; coherent-end formula and its product/Fubini consequence.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-dinatural-section-evaluation] to this $A$ and the coherent section $\xi$ of Step 3. It supplies a single coherent transformation on $C\times\mathcal F$,
$$e_{a,Q}:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F}(A(a),Q)\longrightarrow Q(a),\qquad\alpha\longmapsto\alpha_a(1_a).$$
Its coherence in both $a$ and $Q$ is part of the cited statement. Restrict it along $(l,l')\mapsto(c(l),T(-,l'))$ from $L^{\mathrm{op}}\times L$ to $C\times\mathcal F$, then along $(s,t):\operatorname{Tw}(L)\to L^{\mathrm{op}}\times L$. The source becomes the diagram of inner mapping spaces in Step 2 and the target becomes $D\circ(s,t)$. Thus this construction supplies the actual transformation between the two twisted-arrow diagrams; Hom functoriality alone would not supply it.

source.place: Agent-formulated coherent dinatural-section evaluation pairing, extending the fixed-object comparison of Kerodon Notation 8.3.1.2 (03M4) using coherent ends as in Example 8.3.4.22 (03P7). Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra, construction (5.8.8.4), printed p.257, is the identity-element specialization. These sources do not state the arbitrary-family assertion verbatim. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copies WANTED. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; no Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: For every $a\in C$ and $Q\in\mathcal F$, the covariant clause of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation], with $\mathcal E=C$ and the concrete corepresentable model $A(a)$, says that this very identity-evaluation map $e_{a,Q}$ is an equivalence of whole spaces, with inverse $q\mapsto(f\mapsto Q(f)(q))$. The small-category and small-mapping-space hypotheses hold in the universes of the item. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] to the coherent transformation constructed in Step 4, in a containing universe where $C\times\mathcal F$ is small. It is therefore an equivalence in its functor quasicategory; choose its inverse and two inverse triangles there, so they are coherent in both variables. Restricting preserves this inverse data. Write $e^L:M^L\to D\circ(s,t)$ for this restricted equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Tw}(L),\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$, where $M^L$ is the inner mapping-space diagram of Step 2. [lem-coef-coherent-end-twisted-arrow-formula] supplies a limiting cone $\mu:\Delta y\to M^L$ with $\mathcal V$-small apex $y$. The target $D\circ(s,t)$ is not one of that theorem's mapping-space diagrams, so its limit is obtained by transport: put $\mu'=e^L\circ\mu$. For every space $x$, the map $\operatorname{Map}(x,y)\to\operatorname{Map}(\Delta x,D\circ(s,t))$, $a\mapsto\mu'\circ\Delta a$, is homotopic to $\mu\circ\Delta(-)$ followed by postcomposition with $e^L$ (associativity in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]). The first map is an equivalence because $\mu$ is limiting, and the second because $e^L$ is an equivalence edge with the inverse triangles chosen above ([lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]). By the mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], $\mu'$ is limiting. Hence $\lim D\circ(s,t)$ exists with the same $\mathcal V$-small apex, and the induced map of limits is an equivalence carrying the chosen inverse homotopies. Composing with Step 2 proves the asserted formula.

source.place: Construction (5.8.8.4), Theorem 5.8.9 and Theorem 5.8.13(ii), printed pp.257,259-261; agent expansion separating coherent evaluation from its pointwise invertibility.

proof.text:
The identity-component clause of [lem-coef-coherent-end-twisted-arrow-formula] and the component of $e$ from Step 4 show that projection at $1_l$ is $\tau\mapsto\tau_{c(l),l}(1_{c(l)})$. For a coherent limit point $z$, restrict the inverse equivalence of Step 5 to $1_l$. The inverse formula of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation] gives
$$\tau_{x,l}(f)=T(f,1_l)(z_l).$$
The inverse triangles are those already chosen for a single coherent equivalence and carried through the limit, so this component formula includes the required higher transformation data. Naturality in $T$ and $c$ is obtained by restricting the same coherent evaluation transformation of [lem-coef-dinatural-section-evaluation] along the corresponding families $(c(l),T(-,l'))$; its coherent inverse in Step 5 restricts with it. Restriction of $L$ is precomposition of these diagrams and of their limit cones. The restriction and simplicial-parameter compatibility clauses of the end formula and of the evaluation construction make these comparisons commute with both maps and inverse triangles. The end formula also supplies the $\mathcal V$-small limit model. If $L$ is empty its end and transformation space are terminal; if $C$ is empty, existence of $c$ forces $L$ empty.
